summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul (Democrat) ran again and won re-election over Bruce Blakeman (Republican).

candidates.name: Kathy Hochul
candidates.bio: Kathy Hochul has been governor of New York since 2021. She ran with Adrienne Adams and was also on the Working Families line.

positions.summary: Says she cut middle-class taxes, eliminated taxes on tips, and tripled the state child tax credit.
Counts banning cell phones in schools, universal pre-K and free school meals for every student among her accomplishments.
Defends a one-year statewide moratorium on new hyperscale AI data centers, saying it protects the power grid, water and communities.
Says she protected abortion rights in New York.

candidates.name: Bruce Blakeman
candidates.bio: Bruce Blakeman is the Nassau County Executive. He was also on the Conservative line and ran with Todd Hood.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a pro-choice Republican and says that takes the abortion issue off the table.
Says he wants to cut state income and corporate taxes, not raise them.
Says he would rescind New York's sanctuary state policy on day one.
Opposes the 2019 state climate law and offshore wind, and supports fracking in the Southern Tier to lower energy prices.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Summary originally noted that figures reflected about 95% of returns.
